title: Section 283 — Exhibition of false light, mark or buoy

content.overview: BNS s. 283 — Exhibition of false light, mark or buoy.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Exhibition of false light, mark or buoy. Read with the chapter heading and neighbouring sections. A BNS provision with no single IPC predecessor. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 283 is the rule on “Exhibition of false light, mark or buoy”. The section provides that . Whoever exhibits any false light, mark or buoy, intending or knowing it to be likely that such exhibition will mislead any navigator, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and with fine which shall not be less than ten thousand rupees. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 283 exists so that “Exhibition of false light, mark or buoy” has a closed legal test in Chapter XV — Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Nuisance, adulteration, rash driving, obscenity, lottery.

The provision balances personal liberty with public interest and social order. Modern judicial interpretation emphasizes substantive fairness, proportionality in sentencing, and adherence to constitutional safeguards. distinctions: Section 283 vs General Attempt: Section 283 penalizes the substantive conduct specified in Chapter XV; inchoate attempts without specific provisions fall under the general attempt provisions.

Rule: Under BNS s. 283, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
